description: Holmium is a rare-earth element and the eleventh member of the lanthanide series with atomic number 67. It is a relatively soft, silvery, fairly corrosion-resistant and malleable metal that is too reactive to be found in native form, slowly forming a yellowish oxide coating when exposed to air.
uses: Holmium is used to create the strongest artificially generated magnetic fields when placed within high-strength magnets as a magnetic pole piece. Its compounds are used in certain laser and glass-colorant applications, and it is used as a burnable poison in nuclear reactors due to its strong absorption of neutrons. Glass containing holmium oxide is used as a calibration standard for optical spectrophotometers, and holmium-doped yttrium iron garnet has applications in solid-state lasers and optical isolators.
characteristics: Holmium has the highest magnetic moment (10.6 μB) of any naturally occurring element and the highest magnetic permeability and magnetic saturation of any element. It has a boiling point of 3,000 K and is ferromagnetic below 19 K, and its trivalent ions have fluorescent properties with unique emission light lines that appear yellowish or orange-red depending on lighting conditions.
